issues.display_title: Issue #81: Strip server internals from upload responses
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan G�� Developer

Description

Upload success and error responses expose server internals: storagePath (absolute storage root) in ProjectUpload's 201 body, and storage_path in error bodies of project_upload.go and update_profile.go. Remove them. Clients only need relativePath, fileName, fileUrl, fileSize, fileType.

Why

Absolute filesystem layout is reconnaissance data for an attacker and useless to the FE (a matching FE task switches it to relativePath).

Acceptance Criteria

  • 201 response contains no absolute paths (storagePath removed)
  • Error responses contain no storage_path
  • FE upload, wizard flow, and AI generate still work (coordinate with FE task to consume relativePath)

Dependencies

Depends on #78

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan G�� Developer

Description

Upload validation currently trusts the client-supplied Content-Type multipart header and takes the file extension from the client filename. Replace with server-side checks: sniff actual content via http.DetectContentType (stdlib) on the first 512 bytes, and derive the stored extension from the validated MIME type (map already exists in shared.go) instead of filepath.Ext(filename). Decide SVG policy: drop image/svg+xml from the allowlist, or keep accepting it but serve with Content-Disposition: attachment to neutralize stored-XSS via inline SVG script.

Why

A file that merely claims to be an image passes today's checks. SVG served inline as image/svg+xml can execute script in the user's session (stored XSS).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Genuine PNG/JPEG/WebP uploads succeed
  • A non-image file with a spoofed Content-Type: image/png header is rejected with 400
  • Stored extension always matches detected MIME, regardless of client filename
  • SVG either rejected, or never rendered inline from the file GET endpoint
  • Applies to both project-file upload and avatar upload paths

1. Technical Evaluation & Code Architecture Findings

  • Current Vulnerability in src/action/v1/shared/shared.go: 
    func AllowedImageUpload(fileHeader *multipart.FileHeader) bool {
    if fileHeader == nil {
        return false
    }
    ext := strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(fileHeader.Filename))
    return allowedExts[ext] && AllowedMime(fileHeader.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
}
    The function solely validates filepath.Ext(fileHeader.Filename) and fileHeader.Header.Get("Content-Type"). Because both values originate entirely from client input, an attacker can upload arbitrary scripts, HTML files, or executables by simply spoofing the client headers and extension.
  • Missing Server-Side Content Sniffing:
    Neither project_upload.go nor update_profile.go inspects file content magic bytes via http.DetectContentType (reading the initial 512 bytes).
  • Extension Derivation:
    Stored file extensions are currently derived directly from the client's fileHeader.Filename instead of being mapped from the sniffed, verified MIME type.

User Profile Summary API

Document Paths

  • Branch: product-docs
  • Brainstorming: docs/API/profile/auth_user_profile_summary_brainstorming.md
  • Related profile API: docs/API/auth_me.md
  • Related profile update brainstorming: docs/API/profile/auth_profile_update_brainstorming.md
  • Related billing brainstorming: docs/API/profile/billing/stripe_subscription_billing_brainstorming.md
  • Related screen: User profile settings and account menu

Purpose

Create an API that gives the app the main profile and account summary for the logged-in user.

This API should help the app show the user's identity, subscription plan, password action, and connected GoThru Dashboard account in one clear place.

User Need

A user needs to see their account information without checking several different screens.

The profile area should clearly show who the user is, what plan they have, when the plan renews, whether they should set or change a password, and whether their GoThru Dashboard account is connected.

Expected Experience

When the user opens profile settings or the account menu, the app should request the user's profile summary.

The app should then be able to show:

  • User avatar
  • User full name
  • User email
  • Current subscription plan
  • Subscription renewal date
  • Password action status
  • Connected GoThru Dashboard account information

The summary should only be available after the user is logged in.

User Profile Information

The API should return the user's main profile information:

  • Avatar
  • Full name
  • Email

If the user has no avatar, the avatar value should be empty so the app can show a default profile image, initials, or another fallback.

The full name and email should match the user's current account information.

Subscription Information

The API should return the user's current subscription plan.

Accepted plan values are:

  • Free
  • Basic monthly
  • Basic yearly
  • Pro monthly
  • Pro yearly

The API should also return the subscription renewal date when the user has a paid subscription.

If the user is on the free plan, the renewal date can be empty because the free plan does not renew as a paid subscription.

The app should be able to use this information to show the user's current plan and when the paid plan renews.

Password Action Status

The API should return a status that helps the app decide whether to show a set password action or a change password action.

If the user does not have a password yet, the app should show the set password action.

If the user already has a password, the app should show the change password action.

This status should not expose the user's password.

Connected GoThru Dashboard Account

The API should return connected GoThru Dashboard account information when it exists.

The connected account information should include:

  • Avatar
  • Full name
  • Email
  • Status

Accepted connected account status values are:

  • Connected
  • Expired
  • Failed

Connected means the GoThru Dashboard account is linked and usable.

Expired means the connection exists but needs to be refreshed or reconnected.

Failed means the connection attempt or connection check did not work.

If no GoThru Dashboard account is connected, the API should return a clear empty connected account state.

Business Rules

  • The user must be logged in before viewing the profile summary.
  • The profile summary should only return information for the logged-in user.
  • The user profile section should include avatar, full name, and email.
  • The subscription section should include the current plan.
  • The subscription plan should be one of free, basic monthly, basic yearly, pro monthly, or pro yearly.
  • The subscription section should include a renewal date when the user has a paid subscription.
  • The password status should help the app choose between set password and change password.
  • The password status should never include the actual password.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard account section should include avatar, full name, email, and status when connected account data exists.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard status should be connected, expired, or failed.
  • Missing optional information should be returned clearly so the app can show the right empty state.

Error Cases

The API should return a clear error when:

  • The user is not logged in.
  • The user's profile information cannot be loaded.
  • The user's subscription information cannot be loaded.
  • The user's password action status cannot be determined.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard account information cannot be loaded.

Edge Cases

  • The user has no avatar.
  • The user is on the free plan.
  • The user is on basic monthly.
  • The user is on basic yearly.
  • The user is on pro monthly.
  • The user is on pro yearly.
  • The paid subscription has a renewal date.
  • The free plan has no renewal date.
  • The user does not have a password yet.
  • The user already has a password.
  • The user has no connected GoThru Dashboard account.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard account is connected.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard account is expired.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard account failed.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard account has no avatar.
  • Billing data is temporarily unavailable.
  • GoThru Dashboard connection data is temporarily unavailable.

Success Criteria

This API is successful when:

  • A logged-in user can load their profile summary.
  • Users who are not logged in cannot load a profile summary.
  • The app receives the user's avatar, full name, and email.
  • The app receives the user's subscription plan.
  • The plan is shown as free, basic monthly, basic yearly, pro monthly, or pro yearly.
  • The app receives a subscription renewal date when the user has a paid subscription.
  • The app can show no renewal date for the free plan.
  • The app can decide whether to show set password or change password.
  • The app never receives the actual password.
  • The app receives connected GoThru Dashboard account data when available.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard status is connected, expired, or failed.
  • Empty or missing optional data is handled clearly.
  • The profile settings and account menu can show the right account state without guessing.

Out Of Scope

  • Changing the user's full name.
  • Uploading, changing, or deleting the user's avatar.
  • Setting or changing the user's password.
  • Starting or changing a subscription plan.
  • Processing billing payments.
  • Connecting or reconnecting a GoThru Dashboard account.
  • Editing GoThru Dashboard account data.
  • Returning private password values or payment details.

User Avatar Delete API

Document Paths

  • Branch: product-docs
  • Brainstorming: docs/API/profile/auth_avatar_delete_brainstorming.md
  • Related upload brainstorming: docs/API/profile/auth_avatar_upload_brainstorming.md
  • Related profile API: docs/API/auth_me.md
  • Related screen: User profile settings

Purpose

Create an API that lets a logged-in user delete their profile avatar.

The user should be able to remove their avatar when they no longer want a profile picture shown in the product.

User Need

A user needs a simple way to remove their current profile avatar.

After the avatar is deleted, the user profile should no longer show the old avatar.

The app can then show a default profile image, initials, or another fallback based on the product design.

Expected Experience

When the user opens their profile settings, they should be able to remove their current avatar.

The delete action should only work after the user is logged in.

After a successful delete, the profile should no longer have an avatar path.

The old avatar image should no longer remain in object storage.

Delete Behavior

If the user has an avatar, the API should delete the image data from object storage.

The API should also delete or clear the avatar data saved in the database.

After the delete is complete, the user's profile should behave as if the user has no avatar.

If the user does not have an avatar yet, the API should return a clear result that the profile already has no avatar.

Business Rules

  • The user must be logged in before deleting an avatar.
  • Only the logged-in user can delete their own avatar.
  • The delete action applies only to the user's active profile avatar.
  • The image data should be deleted from object storage.
  • The avatar data should be deleted or cleared from the database.
  • After a successful delete, the profile API should no longer return the old avatar path.
  • Deleting an avatar should not delete the user's account.
  • Deleting an avatar should not change the user's name, email, password, projects, or billing data.

Error Cases

The API should return a clear error when:

  • The user is not logged in.
  • The avatar image cannot be deleted from object storage.
  • The avatar data cannot be deleted or cleared from the database.
  • The saved avatar path is missing or no longer points to an available image.

Edge Cases

  • The user deletes an existing avatar.
  • The user tries to delete an avatar when no avatar is saved.
  • The user starts a delete action but is no longer logged in.
  • Object storage is temporarily unavailable.
  • The database update fails after the object storage delete is attempted.
  • The saved avatar path exists in the database, but the image is already missing from object storage.
  • The user deletes an avatar and then uploads a new avatar soon after.
  • The user opens their profile from another device after the avatar is deleted.

Success Criteria

This API is successful when:

  • A logged-in user can delete their profile avatar.
  • Users who are not logged in cannot delete avatars.
  • A user can only delete their own avatar.
  • The avatar image data is deleted from object storage.
  • The avatar data is deleted or cleared from the database.
  • The profile no longer returns the old avatar path after deletion.
  • The app can show the correct no-avatar state after deletion.
  • A profile with no avatar is handled clearly.
  • Delete errors are clear enough for the app to show helpful messages.

Out Of Scope

  • Uploading a new avatar.
  • Editing, cropping, or resizing an avatar.
  • Deleting another user's avatar.
  • Deleting the user account.
  • Changing the user's name, email, password, projects, or billing data.
  • Managing old avatar history.
